papers.title: Somnus, a tunable, open-source platform for automated EEG sleep scoring in physiological and disease mouse models.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Introduces Somnus, an open-source Python package for automated rodent sleep staging from EEG, EMG, and optional video, built on a base model trained across recordings from six laboratories. Its key contribution is a graphical interface that targets low-certainty epochs for rapid manual correction and fine-tuning, enabling accurate custom scorers for disease models with atypical sleep architecture using only minutes of manual annotation.

papers.title: Isoflurane anesthesia CNS recovery state: ultra-slow oscillations and cellular-stress-responsive gene expression.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Compared recovery from 4 h isoflurane anesthesia with time-matched sleep and sleep deprivation in male C57BL/6J mice using continuous EEG/EMG and frontal cortex RNA sequencing. Isoflurane recovery produced rebound arousal, reduced early NREM/REM sleep, fragmented NREM bouts, and persistent ultra-slow EEG oscillations normalizing within two weeks, with a transcriptomic profile enriched for integrated stress response and unfolded protein response genes distinct from the mTOR-associated profile of sleep deprivation.

papers.title: EEG-SDL-Net: biomedical EEG signal classification via multi-level supervised Kolmogorov-Arnold networks.
papers.summary: Proposes EEG-SDL-Net, a supervised deep learning framework combining hierarchical 1D convolutional networks, Sobel-based temporal enhancement, channel attention, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, and multi-level deep supervision for EEG signal classification. It reports superior accuracy on the SEED-VIG dataset versus state-of-the-art methods and 15 ms real-time inference latency on a Raspberry Pi 4, supporting Edge AI and IoMT deployment.

papers.title: Discrete cortico-hippocampal circuit states underlie mood state transitions in depression.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Using precision functional mapping, large cross-sectional cohorts, and intracranial EEG, shows hippocampal connectivity alternates between discrete DMN-dominant and sensorimotor-dominant network states on the order of minutes. In major depressive disorder the DMN-dominant state is overrepresented, hippocampus-DMN coupling tracks symptom fluctuations, and electroconvulsive therapy shifts connectivity toward the SM-dominant state in association with positive treatment response.

papers.title: Alpha-range neural oscillations are associated with multiple dynamic brain networks.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Tested in two independent resting-state EEG-fMRI datasets (n=94 discovery, n=33 replication) whether alpha-range (8-12 Hz) oscillations associate with dynamic BOLD coactivation patterns. Low-alpha periods were mainly linked to unique dCAPs involving visual cortex, sensorimotor and attention networks plus posterior thalamus, while overlapping default, control, and attention network dCAPs occurred in both low- and high-alpha periods, supporting a dynamic gating framework for alpha.

papers.title: Coupled neuro-fluid dynamics in human bioelectromagnetism.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using conductive-fluid phantom experiments, structural MRI, and in vivo EEG/MEG recordings, this study challenges the assumption that tissue and CSF are passive volume conductors. Mechanically driven fluid produced structured, source-localizable oscillatory electromagnetic signals resembling M/EEG, and interindividual CSF volume moderated M/EEG amplitude, suggesting coupled neuro-fluid dynamics.

papers.title: Cortical physiological arousal following termination of absence seizures.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Analyzing scalp EEG from 55 patients across four cohorts, this study found that absence seizure offset was followed by a broadband gamma (>25 Hz) and delta (<4 Hz) power increase decaying over 15-30 s, rather than immediate return to baseline. This suggests postictal recovery is an active arousal process with a characteristic electrophysiological signature.

papers.title: Two-stage spatiotemporal graph neural network framework for seizure onset zone localization.
papers.summary: The authors propose a two-stage, uncertainty-aware framework combining patient-specific spatiotemporal graph neural networks with cross-patient probabilistic ranking to localize the seizure onset zone from intracranial EEG. In a 36-patient bi-institutional cohort, SOZ electrodes were prioritized among top-ranked contacts in good-outcome patients (AUC = .86 ± .06), with reduced spatial separability in poor-outcome patients.

papers.title: Altered EEG-derived co-fluctuation structure in disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: This study adapted an EEG-derived co-fluctuation framework to resting-state data, decomposing connectivity time series into high- and low-amplitude frames to characterize dynamic functional connectivity across consciousness levels. Loss of consciousness was associated with reduced co-fluctuation stability, a shift toward random system dynamics, and reduced spatial and temporal heterogeneity, with combined HAF/LAF parameters showing diagnostic potential for distinguishing DOC states.

papers.title: Faster peak alpha frequency precedes higher menstrual pain in adolescence.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Using longitudinal 64-channel EEG in adolescents before and after menarche, this study found that those later reporting higher menstrual pain already showed faster occipital peak alpha frequency before their first period, a difference persisting post-menarche. Oscillatory power and functional connectivity did not differ by pain group, suggesting peak alpha frequency may be an early susceptibility trait.

papers.title: Understanding Performance Plateaus and Representation Collapse in 3D MRI Transformers Trained to Classify Brain Disease.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Spectral analysis of supervised 3D vision transformers classifying Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative brain MRI showed that discriminative signal is compressed into a single dominant principal component (EVR@1 = 0.90–0.96), producing representation collapse and performance plateaus as training data increase. This spike was 11–26 times larger than predicted for supervised encoders but absent for the frozen self-supervised DINO encoder (0.66), and plateauing tracked the learned encoder rather than task difficulty.

papers.title: Probing the neural geometry of conscious object perception in time.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: High-density EEG during a threshold-level object recognition task revealed early (~100 ms) emergence of both basic- and superordinate-level category information, with basic-level category positively and superordinate-level negatively correlated with perceptual awareness. An abstract superordinate representation emerged later (~300 ms) and positively correlated with awareness, supporting a basic-to-superordinate sequence in conscious object perception.

papers.title: Altered interictal alpha-band organization in childhood absence epilepsy.
papers.summary: Eyes-closed resting EEG in 49 drug-naive children with childhood absence epilepsy versus 83 controls showed lower individual alpha frequency (8.80 vs 9.42 Hz) and reduced posterior predominance of phase-lagged synchronization at 12 Hz (baseline-subtracted frontal-posterior log-ratio difference 0.332, Hedges' g = 0.79). Circular-shift surrogate baselines largely removed the controls' posterior predominance, and the contrast was smaller at individual alpha frequency.

papers.title: Sleep as a vulnerability marker in clinical high-risk populations. a multimodal systematic review.
papers.summary: PRISMA-guided systematic review of 26 studies found sleep disturbances in 59–80% of clinical high-risk individuals, with actigraphy predicting 12-month positive symptom worsening and polysomnographic markers (reduced prefrontal spindle duration, elevated NREM gamma power, reduced slow wave density) replicated across cohorts. Whole-thalamus–DLPFC hypoconnectivity was identified as a convergent thalamocortical marker.

papers.title: Depressive status modulates hippocampal-cortical dynamics during acute nicotine use.
papers.summary: Using simultaneous hippocampal responsive neurostimulation electrodes and scalp EEG in two chronic nicotine users, one with and one without depression, this study found that oscillatory activity tracked mood only in the non-depressed individual, whereas both showed reduced alpha hippocampal-cortical connectivity after nicotine inhalation. The authors interpret this as preliminary evidence that depressive status may modulate nicotine-driven network dynamics.

papers.title: Aging Is Associated with Reduced Topographic Differentiation Between Speaking and Silent Reading.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: EEG comparison of 15 young and 15 older adults during speaking versus silent reading found similar global field power across groups but greater global dissimilarity index in young adults during later intervals (508–629 and 660–800 ms), indicating reduced neural differentiation between tasks with aging. Behavioral performance and correlations with digit span or speech onset time were not significant.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-generated and algorithmically personalized music interventions and their effects on brain function, behavior, and health: a critical review.
papers.summary: This critical review synthesized 21 studies of algorithmically personalized and AI-generated music interventions and found very low certainty evidence overall, with the most consistent neurophysiological signal from closed-loop neural systems (e.g., music-based alpha neurofeedback producing higher normalized alpha power than yoked random feedback). All eight comparator studies favored the algorithmic condition, but designs were heterogeneous and no finding was independently replicated, so the evidence supports further investigation rather than clinical deployment.

papers.title: Ion Channels and Morphology Drive Widespread Resonance in Human Cortical Interneurons.
papers.summary: Combining Patch-seq, acute electrophysiology, organotypic cultures, and computational modeling, this study found that membrane potential resonance is more prevalent in adult human cortical interneurons than in mouse interneurons, peaking in parvalbumin cells and correlating with low input resistance, voltage sag, and HCN1, KCNJ16, and CACNA1A expression. HCN blockade abolished resonance, and models showed human morphology and ion channels sharpen frequency tuning under in vivo-like noisy conditions.

papers.title: Self-Guided Beta-Responsive Visual Neurofeedback in a Public Exhibition: Feasibility and Usability Randomized Controlled rial.
papers.summary: In a single-session two-arm randomized feasibility and usability trial at a public science exhibition, an autonomous consumer-EEG beta-responsive visual neurofeedback system was completed with valid recordings by 71.8% of starters and achieved good usability (mean SUS 72.3); adding a fixed 6 breaths/minute breathing pacer did not improve usability, relaxation, or state mindfulness. Higher resting beta showed a preliminary uncorrected association with lower perceived usability.

papers.title: Social Media Use and Emotional Reactivity to Negative Stimuli: An ERP Investigation.
papers.summary: In 56 healthy young adults, EEG event-related potentials to IAPS emotional images showed larger late positive potential (LPP) amplitudes to negative versus neutral and positive images, while early posterior negativity did not differ by valence. High versus low social media users showed no group differences in these neural responses, suggesting intact emotional engagement rather than desensitization.

papers.title: Sensorimotor expertise effects extend from dance to face perception.
papers.summary: Comparing 26 dancers and 26 non-dancers using visual and somatosensory evoked potentials during a facial emotion and sex discrimination task, the study found expertise-related differences in visual and somatosensory processing of emotional faces. Dancers showed early somatosensory emotion effects (P50) and task-modulated later somatosensory engagement, whereas non-dancers showed more lateralized visual emotion differentiation and later localized somatosensory effects.

papers.title: Functional and Structural Neuroanatomic Correlates of Intraoperative Anesthetic Dose-Adjusted EEG Alpha Power Among Older Surgical Patients.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In the ALADDIN prospective cohort of 168 older non-cardiac/non-cranial surgery patients, lower anesthetic dose-adjusted frontoparietal EEG alpha power was associated with altered default mode, dorsal attention, and salience network connectivity, lower cortical thickness in occipitotemporal and superior parietal cortices, and greater postoperative delirium incidence and severity. These findings suggest functional and structural neuroanatomic bases for altered anesthetic alpha responses and delirium risk.

papers.title: Conserved Thalamic Astrocytic Pathology in Mice and Patients Links TBI to Epilepsy.
papers.summary: Combining mouse multimodal imaging, electrophysiology, and neuropathology with human imaging and postmortem analyses, this study identifies a conserved thalamocortical phenotype in post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE). PTE-prone mice and PTE patients showed disproportionate thalamic atrophy, reduced thalamic radiation fractional anisotropy, and astrocytic reactivity/simplification with impaired glutamate-homeostasis proteins arising before spontaneous seizures, whereas microglial reactivity did not distinguish PTE.

papers.title: Repetitive clustered low-voltage fast activity on intracranial electroencephalogram in mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia and epilepsy: A candidate electroencephalographic biomarker study.
papers.summary: In retrospective multicenter iEEG recordings, the authors identified stereotyped clusters of brief low-voltage fast activity (LVFA) recurring in status-like episodes that occurred in 16 of 18 MOGHE patients and no non-MOGHE patients. Blinded validation classified 10 of 11 MOGHE and 10 of 11 non-MOGHE cases correctly (90.9% agreement), and resection of LVFA-cluster territory was associated with postsurgical seizure freedom.

papers.title: Abnormal SEP recovery amongst multimodal electrophysiological studies to indicate cortical dysfunction in PME.
papers.summary: In 11 adult progressive myoclonic epilepsy (PME) patients versus 11 matched controls, multimodal electrophysiology showed increased N20/P25 SEP amplitudes, prolonged P14/N18/P25 latencies, and abnormal SEP recovery with marked attenuation at the shortest interstimulus interval followed by rapid recovery. Blink reflex R2 latencies were prolonged with increased amplitudes, while MEP parameters did not differ significantly, indicating impaired somatosensory inhibitory processing with relative preservation of corticospinal excitability.

papers.title: EEG responses to monosodium glutamate concentration and individual umami sensitivity in healthy adults.
papers.summary: Combined psychophysics with 64-channel EEG in 38 healthy adults to examine cortical responses to monosodium glutamate concentration versus individual detection-threshold sensitivity. Increasing MSG concentration reduced fronto-central P200 and posterior N200 amplitudes and weakened right orbitofrontal-dorsolateral prefrontal beta-band connectivity, while individual sensitivity could not be decoded above chance.

papers.title: A Human iPSC-Derived Neuron and Glioma Culture Model Reveals Increased Neuronal Excitability and Loss of GABAergic Inhibition.
papers.summary: Established a human iPSC-derived culture of glutamatergic neurons, GABAergic neurons, and astrocytes with and without glioma cells, characterized by immunocytochemistry, multi-electrode arrays, and patch-clamp. Glioma co-culture increased spike rate and network activity and reversed muscimol suppression into elevation of firing, indicating disrupted GABAergic inhibition and increased glutamatergic neuron excitability.

papers.title: Cellularized, needle-deployed intracortical arrays for brain electrophysiology.
papers.summary: Presents a hybrid implantation method combining a cellularized hydrogel with a neural recording array for simultaneous needle delivery into the brain. Post-implantation electrophysiological recordings demonstrated functional integration with surrounding neural tissue, supporting feasibility for coupled bioelectronic sensing and regenerative capability.

papers.title: Large-scale all-optical electrophysiology links excitability and connectivity to circuit dynamics in vivo.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Developed large-scale all-optical electrophysiology and applied it to about 300 layer 1 interneurons per mouse in vivo, identifying 1,469 inhibitory and 5,752 directed electrical connections across 14,312 tested pairs. Presynaptic identity related more to IPSP amplitude and postsynaptic identity more to IPSP decay, and measured intrinsic excitability predicted spontaneous spiking features.

papers.title: The 1st Rzeszów Electroencephalography Days: An educational review and future perspectives.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: An educational review accompanying the 1st Rzeszów Electroencephalography Days, summarizing EEG topics and offering future perspectives; no abstract was supplied, so specific findings cannot be stated.

papers.title: Voltage versus concentration in ion channels: Physical signatures reveal rate-limiting steps.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Shows that voltage- and chemical-potential-driven ion flux produce distinct current-voltage signatures because voltage alters transition rates throughout the permeation pathway while chemical potential mainly changes ion uptake probabilities. Proposes a three-measurement I-V protocol to identify the rate-limiting step, and applying it to KcsA data identifies release as rate-limiting for outward permeation.

papers.title: Comparison of Commercial Fixed and In-House Tissue-Based and Live Cell-Based Assays for the Detection of Common Neuronal Surface Autoantibodies.
papers.summary: Compared commercial fixed-cell CBAs with in-house live-cell CBAs and tissue-based assays in 45 patients positive for NMDAR, LGI1, or CASPR2 antibodies. Live CBA/TBA showed higher diagnostic accuracy and reduced false positives, with positivity aligning with definite autoimmune encephalitis criteria, though live CBA and neurofilament light chain did not predict immunotherapy response or coexisting cancer.

papers.title: A subtype-specific gene regulatory program controls differential circuit integration of deep CA3 pyramidal neurons
papers.summary: Combining developmental single-nucleus multiomics with genetic targeting, morphology, and electrophysiology, this study identified the transcription factor ST18 as a regulator of deep CA3 pyramidal neuron subtype identity that represses a superficial-associated program. Postnatal ST18 loss shifted deep CA3 neurons toward a superficial-like transcriptional and chromatin state, with increased thorny excrescence elaboration, enhanced excitatory synaptic activity, and reduced burst-firing.

papers.title: Excitation-contraction coupling plasticity is revealed upon RyR2 depletion in adult mouse ventricular myocytes.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Used an adult tamoxifen-inducible RyR2 conditional knockout mouse to test whether excitation-contraction coupling adapts to acute RyR2 loss. Hearts with <10% residual RyR2 maintained normal structure, function, Ca2+ transient amplitude, and ECC gain via elevated SR Ca2+ load, high channel reserve, and CaT autoregulation, revealing intrinsic ECC plasticity.

papers.title: 5-HT1A Antagonist WAY-100635 Prevents Chronic Neurodegeneration and Immune Activation After TBI.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Tested post-injury WAY-100635, a 5-HT1A antagonist, in mice after controlled cortical impact and found it preserved retinal ganglion cell survival and visual function, maintained visually evoked cortical responses, and reduced microglial activation and reactive astrogliosis. Treatment also improved early motor performance and reduced injury-associated behavioral disinhibition without significantly reducing cortical cavity volume.

papers.title: Cardiac electrophysiology procedures must be performed exclusively by trained electrophysiologists: A statement from the Heart Rhythm Society and Heart Rhythm Advocates.
papers.summary: Presents an evidence-based Heart Rhythm Society/Heart Rhythm Advocates position statement arguing that cardiac electrophysiology procedures should be performed exclusively by fellowship-trained clinical cardiac electrophysiologists. Cites outcome data and registry analyses showing operator specialization is a strong independent predictor of procedural safety and long-term outcomes.

papers.title: The ligament of Marshall as a therapeutic target in atrial fibrillation: from anatomy to catheter-based and surgical management-a narrative review.
keywords: ethanol infusion of vein of Marshall
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes anatomical, electrophysiological and clinical evidence on the ligament of Marshall as an atrial fibrillation target, comparing percutaneous ethanol infusion into the vein of Marshall (EIVOM) with thoracoscopic surgical division. Pooled analysis of five randomized EIVOM trials (>1,100 patients) showed improved 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia (RR 1.16, 95% CI 1.04-1.29; NNT 10) without excess major complications, though no trial tested ethanol infusion in isolation and surgical division lacks randomized evidence.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
